eventMetadata.context_description: Current forecasts from the Korea Meteorological Administration and international models point to a daytime high near 24–25 °C in Busan on June 7, driven by persistent cloud cover, light showers, and moderate southwesterly flow that limits daytime heating. Early June climatology shows average highs of 23–26 °C along the southeastern coast, where the East Sea’s marine layer and typical humidity suppress rapid warming. The closely matched market probabilities around 24 °C and 25 °C reflect this narrow ensemble range, with slight downside risk from additional rain and upside limited by the absence of strong high-pressure ridging or clear skies. Updated model runs tomorrow morning will determine whether the peak edges toward 26 °C or stays capped below 25 °C.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 7 Jun '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/ph/manila/RPLL.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official PAGASA forecasts for Metro Manila on June 7 project a daily high near 32°C under partly cloudy to cloudy skies with a 40-60% chance of isolated rain showers or thunderstorms, aligning closely with the long-term June climatological average. The southwest monsoon season brings elevated humidity and frequent convective activity that typically caps afternoon peaks around this threshold, though reduced cloud cover or delayed rainfall could allow brief warming to 33°C. Market-implied odds reflect this tight balance, with traders weighting the most probable outcomes based on ensemble model consensus and historical analogs for early June conditions. Resolution hinges on the official maximum temperature recorded by PAGASA instrumentation.
